**A Gentle, Step‑by‑Step Checklist for Getting Your Papers in Order** *(Designed for someone who wants everything clear and easy for loved ones after they’re gone. Feel free to print it, tick boxes as you go, and keep a copy in a safe place — ​e.g., a fire‑proof box, a trusted attorney’s office, or with a designated family member.)* --- ### 1. Legal Foundations | ☐ | Item | What to Do | Where to Store / Who Should Know | |---|------|------------|----------------------------------| | ☐ | **Last Will & Testament** | • Draft or update with an estate‑planning attorney.
• Name an executor (person who will administer the estate).
• Specify guardianship for any dependents (if applicable) and specific bequests (e.g., your father’s watch, tools, cat). | • Original with attorney.
• Copy in your safe‑deposit box or home safe.
• Inform executor and a trusted friend/neighbor of its location. | | ☐ | **Durable Power of Attorney (POA) – Financial** | • Appoint someone you trust to manage finances if you become incapacitated.
• Define scope (banking, bills, property, investments). | • Original with attorney.
• Copy given to your POA holder; keep a copy in your personal files. | | ☐ | **Durable Power of Attorney – Health Care (or Advance Directive)** | • Name a health‑care agent.
• Include wishes about life‑support, resuscitation, organ donation, etc. | • Same storage as financial POA.
• Give a copy to your primary physician and the appointed agent. | | ☐ | **Living Will / Advance Health Care Directive** | • Clarify end‑of‑life treatment preferences (e.g., palliative care, hospice). | • With health‑care POA; also keep a copy in your medical file. | | ☐ | **Beneficiary Designations** (retirement accounts, life insurance, payable‑on‑death bank accounts) | • Review and update beneficiaries to reflect current wishes.
• Ensure they align with your will (avoid contradictions). | • Keep a list with your will; inform your executor. | | ☐ | **Trust Documents** (if you have a revocable living trust) | • Verify funding (assets transferred into trust).
• Name successor trustee. | • Original with attorney; copy in safe place. | | ☐ | **Letter of Instruction** (non‑legal but helpful) | • Explain where to find important items, passwords, pet care wishes, funeral preferences, etc.
• Not a substitute for a will, but reduces guesswork. | • Keep with your will; tell executor where it is. | --- ### 2. Financial & Banking Records | ☐ | Item | What to Do | Where to Store / Who Should Know | |---|------|------------|----------------------------------| | ☐ | **Bank & Credit Union Statements** (last 12 months) | • Gather checking, savings, CDs, money‑market accounts.
• Note account numbers, online login info (store securely). | • Physical folder or encrypted digital folder.
• Share login details with POA holder via a password manager (e.g., LastPass, 1Password) or a sealed envelope. | | ☐ | **Investment Accounts** (brokerage, IRA, 401(k), pension) | • List each institution, account #, current balance, beneficiary.
• Include any stock certificates or bonds. | • Same as bank statements.
• Inform your executor and POA. | | ☐ | **Debt & Liabilities** (mortgage, car loan, credit cards, personal loans) | • List each creditor, account #, outstanding balance, monthly payment.
• Note any automatic payments. | • Keep with financial statements.
• POA should know to stop or transfer payments. | | ☐ | **Tax Returns** (last 3‑7 years) | • Federal, state, local.
• Include supporting documents (W‑2s, 1099s, deduction records). | • Store in a labeled folder; executor may need them for final filing. | | ☐ | **Insurance Policies** (life, health, homeowners/renters, auto, long‑term care) | • Policy #, insurer, coverage amount, beneficiary.
• Note premium due dates. | • Keep with financial records.
• Inform executor and POA. | | ☐ | **Property Deeds & Titles** (home, vehicle, boat, etc.) | • Locate original deed/title; note any liens. | • Safe‑deposit box or fire‑proof safe.
• Copy with executor. | | ☐ | **Valuable Personal Property List** (watch, tools, jewelry, art, collectibles) | • Description, photos, approximate value, location.
• Note any items you wish to give to specific people (e.g., father’s watch to neighbor). | • Attach to Letter of Instruction; keep a copy with will. | | ☐ | **Digital Assets** (email, social media, cloud storage, crypto wallets, domain names) | • List usernames, URLs, and instructions for access or closure.
• Use a secure password manager and share the master password with POA/executor. | • Store the master password in a sealed envelope with your will or in your attorney’s safe. | --- ### 3. Personal & Family Matters | ☐ | Item | What to Do | Where to Store / Who Should Know | |---|------|------------|----------------------------------| | ☐ | **Pet Care Instructions** (for your cat) | • Daily routine, vet contact, food preferences, medication.
• Name the neighbor you asked to look after the cat and any backup caregiver. | • Include in Letter of Instruction; give a copy to the neighbor. | | ☐ | **Funeral / Memorial Wishes** | • Burial vs. cremation, preferred cemetery, service details, music, readings, donations in lieu of flowers.
• Pre‑paid arrangements (if any). | • Keep with Letter of Instruction; inform executor and a close friend. | | ☐ | **Important Contacts List** | • Family, friends, attorney, financial advisor, physician, clergy, insurance agent, etc.
• Phone numbers and email addresses. | • Printed copy in your personal file; digital copy in password manager. | | ☐ | **Military Service Records** (if applicable) | • DD‑214, medals, pension info. | • With personal documents; may be needed for veterans’ benefits. | | ☐ | **Organ Donor / Body Donation Registration** | • Confirm registration status; keep confirmation card or PDF. | • With health‑care advance directive. | --- ### 4. Safe Storage & Communication Plan 1. **Primary Safe Location** – Fire‑proof home safe or a safety‑deposit box at your bank. - Store: original will, POAs, trust deed, property titles, insurance policies, Letter of Instruction, and a USB drive with encrypted digital copies. 2. **Secondary Copies** – Give a **set of copies** (not originals) to: - Your named executor. - Your financial POA holder. - A trusted friend or neighbor (e.g., the one you asked to watch your cat). 3. **Digital Backup** – Encrypted external hard drive or secure cloud service (e.g., Tresorit, Sync.com). Share the encryption key only with executor/POA. 4. **Review Schedule** – Set a calendar reminder to **review and update** every 12 months or after any major life change (new asset, change in health, marriage, death of a beneficiary, etc.). 5. **Inform Key People** – Have a brief conversation (or leave a note) with: - Executor: “My will is in the safe‑deposit box; the key is with my attorney.” - POA holder: “You’ll find the financial folder in the top drawer of my desk; the password manager master key is in the envelope marked ‘POA.’” - Neighbor/cat caregiver: “If I’m away long‑term, please feed, water, and take my cat to Dr. Smith; the vet’s contact is on the fridge.” --- ### 5. Quick‑Reference One‑Page Summary (Print & Post) ``` ☐ Will & Executor ☐ Financial POA (name: __________) ☐ Health‑Care POA / Advance Directive ☐ Beneficiary designations (IRA, life insurance, etc.) ☐ Letter of Instruction (location: __________) ☐ Bank & investment account list (with login info) ☐ Debts & liabilities list ☐ Tax returns (last 3‑7 yr) ☐ Insurance policies (life, home, auto, etc.) ☐ Property deeds & titles ☐ Personal property list (watch, tools, cat care) ☐ Digital assets & password manager info ☐ Pet care instructions (cat) ☐ Funeral / memorial wishes ☐ Important contacts list ☐ Storage location: __________ (safe/deposit box) ☐ Copies given to: Executor __________, POA __________, Neighbor __________ ☐ Review date: __________ (annual) ``` Print this, tick each box as you complete the step, and keep the page with your will or in your personal planner. --- ### Final Thoughts - **Professional Help:** Even a simple will benefits from an attorney’s review to avoid unintended gaps or contradictions. A certified financial planner can help align beneficiary designations with your estate plan. - **Emotional Support:** Sorting these papers can feel overwhelming. Consider doing a little each day, or ask a trusted friend to sit with you while you work through the list. - **Your Legacy:** By taking these steps now, you’re giving yourself peace of mind and sparing loved ones from guesswork during a difficult time. If you’d like a template for any of the documents (e.g., a simple Letter of Instruction or a Personal Property Inventory), just let me know — I’m happy to provide one. Wishing you strength and clarity as you work through this. 🌿
